summary.short: Austrian statute requiring profit-oriented providers of large communication platforms to run notice-and-takedown and review procedures for unlawful content, publish reports, appoint a responsible officer, and face KommAustria supervision and fines, from 1 January 2021.
summary.long: The Kommunikationsplattformen-Gesetz (KoPl-G) applies to domestic and foreign profit-oriented providers of communication platforms, except where both user numbers are under 100,000 and Austrian turnover is under EUR 500,000. It also excludes marketplaces, non-profit encyclopedias, educational platforms and media outlets, and video-sharing platforms for their broadcasts and user videos. Providers must run an effective, transparent notice procedure: remove or block manifestly unlawful content within 24 hours and other unlawful content within seven days, preserve removed content and identifying data for up to ten weeks, and offer a review procedure with a two-week application period. They must publish reports, half-yearly above one million registered users, and appoint a responsible officer and a service agent. Users may complain to a complaints body (Beschwerdestelle) supported by RTR-GmbH. KommAustria supervises compliance, may order providers by decision to restore lawful conditions, and may impose fines of up to EUR 10 million for listed breaches, up to EUR 1 million for failing to appoint a responsible officer after a request, and up to EUR 58,000 for refusing information. Measures may not amount to general ex-ante content control. The Act entered into force on 1 January 2021, and existing providers had until 31 March 2021 to comply.

relations.note: The header records the parliamentary materials for the enacting Act; the document itself is the Bundesgesetzblatt publication.

notes: Text version: the original as adopted (BGBl. I Nr. 151/2020, issued 23 Dec 2020), extent full; no consolidated version was provided. The registry status 'repealed' is not supported by the document, which contains no repeal provision, so no repeal relation or event is recorded here. Internal points: § 14 sets a 31 March 2021 compliance deadline for existing providers and three months from the start of activity for later ones. § 3 Abs. 3 Z 1 sets 24-hour and seven-day removal periods, while § 4 Abs. 2 Z 7 asks for reporting bands that include 72 hours, which § 3 does not set. The Act names no enabling act; its only execution clause is § 13 (Bundeskanzler).

thresholds.variable_text: Anzahl der mittels Registrierung für die Kommunikationsplattform zugangsberechtigten Nutzer in Österreich
thresholds.measurement: Average over the preceding calendar year; number of users with registration-based access in Austria
thresholds.consequence: Provider is outside the Act's scope if this user threshold is below 100,000 and the revenue threshold in § 1 Abs. 2 Z 2 is also met.
thresholds.conditions: Joint condition with § 1 Abs. 2 Z 2 (revenue below EUR 500,000); both must be met for the exclusion.

thresholds.variable_text: der mit dem Betrieb der Kommunikationsplattform im vorangegangenen Kalenderjahr in Österreich erzielte Umsatz
thresholds.measurement: Revenue earned in Austria from operating the platform in the preceding calendar year
thresholds.consequence: Provider is outside the Act's scope if this revenue threshold is below EUR 500,000 and the user threshold in § 1 Abs. 2 Z 1 is also met.
thresholds.conditions: Joint condition with § 1 Abs. 2 Z 1 (fewer than 100,000 registered users in Austria); both must be met for the exclusion.
